claim: LPLC2 neurons have dendrites in the lobula and the four layers of the lobula plate (LP): LP1, LP2, LP3, and LP4.
source: (A) An LPLC2 neuron has dendrites in lobula and the four layers of the lobula plate (LP): LP1, LP2, LP3, and LP4.
evidence: This is stated directly in the figure caption and shown in the anatomical diagram in Figure 1A.

claim: The four branches of LPLC2 dendrites align with the preferred motion directions in the corresponding LP layers.
source: Moreover, the physical extensions of the LPLC2 dendrites align with the preferred motion directions in the corresponding LP layers (Figure 1B; Klapoetke et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citation to Klapoetke et al., 2017.

claim: Each LP layer uniquely receives motion information in one of the four cardinal directions.
source: The retinotopic LP layers host the axon terminals of motion detection neurons, and each layer uniquely receives motion information in one of the four cardinal directions (Maisak et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citation to Maisak et al., 2013.

claim: LPLC2 dendrites form an outward radial structure that matches the moving edges of a looming object expanding from the receptive field center.
source: These dendrites form an outward radial structure, which matches the moving edges of a looming object that expands from the receptive field center (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: A population of more than 200 LPLC2 neurons converges onto the giant fibers.
source: The axons of a population of more than 200 LPLC2 neurons converge to the giant fibers, descending neurons that mediate escape behaviors (Ache et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption with citation to Ache et al., 2019.

claim: When an object is on a straight-line collision course with an animal, its edges appear to expand radially outward.
source: When an object is on a straight-line collision course with an animal, its edges will appear to the observer to expand radially outward, gradually occupying a larger and larger portion of the visual field (Video 1).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text describing the visual characteristics of collision-course objects.

claim: An object heading toward the animal but not colliding with it expands with respect to the object's center rather than radially outward.
source: An object heading toward the animal, but which will not collide with it, also expands to occupy an increasing portion of the visual field, but its edges do not expand radially outwards with respect to the observer. Instead, they expand with respect to the object's center so that opposite edges can move in the same direction across the retina (Video 2).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text describing non-collision trajectories.

claim: Training anatomically-constrained shallow neural networks to detect collisions results in two distinct, opposing solutions.
source: Surprisingly, the optimization arrives at two distinct, opposing solutions, only one of which matches the actual dendritic weighting of LPLC2 neurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract.

claim: Only one of the two optimized solutions matches the actual dendritic weighting of LPLC2 neurons.
source: Surprisingly, the optimization arrives at two distinct, opposing solutions, only one of which matches the actual dendritic weighting of LPLC2 neurons.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a key finding.

claim: Both optimized solutions can solve the collision detection inference problem with high accuracy when the population size is large enough.
source: Both solutions can solve the inference problem with high accuracy when the population size is large enough.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: The LPLC2-like solutions reproduce experimentally observed LPLC2 neuron responses for many stimuli.
source: The LPLC2-like solutions reproduces experimentally observed LPLC2 neuron responses for many stimuli, and reproduces canonical tuning of loom sensitive neurons, even though the models are never trained on neural data.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a key result.

claim: The optimized models reproduce canonical tuning of loom sensitive neurons despite never being trained on neural data.
source: The LPLC2-like solutions reproduces experimentally observed LPLC2 neuron responses for many stimuli, and reproduces canonical tuning of loom sensitive neurons, even though the models are never trained on neural data.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the abstract.

claim: LPLC2 neuron properties and tuning are predicted by optimizing an anatomically-constrained neural network to detect impending collisions.
source: Thus, LPLC2 neuron properties and tuning are predicted by optimizing an anatomically-constrained neural network to detect impending collisions.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract.

claim: Many species from insects to humans rely on visual cues to identify approaching or looming objects.
source: Many species, from insects to humans, rely on a range of visual cues to identify approaching, or looming, objects (Regan and Beverley, 1978; Sun and Frost, 1998; Gabbiani et al., 1999; Card and Dickinson, 2008; Münch et al., 2009; Temizer et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated directly with multiple citations supporting the claim.

claim: LPLC2 neurons send their axons to descending neurons called giant fibers (GFs).
source: These neurons tile visual space, sending their axons to descending neurons called the giant fibers (GFs), which trigger the fly's jumping and take-off behaviors (Tanouye and Wyman, 1980; Card and Dickinson, 2008; von Reyn et al., 2017; Ache et al., 2019).
evidence: This is directly stated with citations.

claim: Giant fibers trigger the fly's jumping and take-off behaviors.
source: These neurons tile visual space, sending their axons to descending neurons called the giant fibers (GFs), which trigger the fly's jumping and take-off behaviors (Tanouye and Wyman, 1980; Card and Dickinson, 2008; von Reyn et al., 2017; Ache et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated directly with supporting citations.

claim: Strong inhibition for inward-directed motion suppresses LPLC2 responses to stimuli that only partially match the radial structure.
source: Common stimuli such as the wide-field motion generated by movement of the insect only match part of the radial structure, and strong inhibition for inward-directed motion suppresses responses to such stimuli.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text describing LPLC2 function.

claim: The structure of LPLC2 dendrites favors responses to visual stimuli with edges moving radially outwards.
source: Thus, the structure of the LPLC2 dendrites favors responses to visual stimuli with edges moving radially outwards, corresponding to objects approaching the receptive field center.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the anatomical description.

claim: Optimization finds two distinct types of solutions with spatial structures that are roughly opposite from one another.
source: After training with 200 random initializations of the filters, we find that the converged solutions fall into three broad categories (Figure 5, Figure 5—figure supplement 1). Two solutions have spatial structures that are—surprisingly—roughly opposite from one another (magenta and green).
evidence: This is stated directly as a finding from the training experiments.

claim: Outward solutions have excitatory components that resemble the dendritic structures of actual LPLC2 neurons.
source: Units with outward-oriented filters are activated by motion radiating outwards from the center of the receptive field, such as the hit event illustrated in Figure 3. These excitatory components resemble the dendritic structures of the actual LPLC2 neurons observed in experiments, where for example, the rightward motion-sensitive component (LP2) occupies mainly the right side of the receptive field.
evidence: This is stated directly comparing model results to experimental observations.

claim: In outward solutions of LRF models, the rightward motion-sensitive inhibitory components mainly occupy the left side of the receptive field.
source: In the outward solutions of the LRF models, the rightward motion-sensitive inhibitory components mainly occupy the left side of the receptive field (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated directly with reference to figures showing the filter structure.

claim: The inhibitory component structure in outward solutions is consistent with properties of lobula plate intrinsic (LPi) interneurons.
source: This is also consistent with the properties of the lobula plate intrinsic (LPi) interneurons, which project inhibitory signals roughly retinotopically from one LP layer to the adjacent layer with opposite directional tuning (Mauss et al., 2015; Klapoetke et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citations to experimental work on LPi neurons.

claim: Inward solutions have the rightward sensitive excitatory component occupying the left side of the receptive field.
source: In the inward solutions, the rightward sensitive excitatory component occupies the left side of the receptive field, and the inhibitory component occupies the right side.
evidence: This is stated directly describing the inward solution structure.

claim: Inward solutions make the model selective for motion converging toward the receptive field center.
source: Such weightings make the model selective for motion converging toward the receptive field center, such as the retreat event shown in Figure 3.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the filter structure.

claim: The baseline activity of outward units is zero when there is no signal.
source: When there is no signal, the baseline activity of outward units is zero; however, the baseline activity of inward units is above zero (grey dashed lines in Figure 7B and C).
evidence: This is stated directly with reference to figure panels.

claim: The baseline activity of inward units is above zero when there is no signal.
source: When there is no signal, the baseline activity of outward units is zero; however, the baseline activity of inward units is above zero (grey dashed lines in Figure 7B and C).
evidence: This is stated directly with reference to figure panels.

claim: Inward units are sensitive to hit stimuli coming from the edges of the receptive field rather than from the center.
source: This helps explain why the inward units can act as loom detectors: they are sensitive to hit stimuli coming from the edges of the receptive field rather than from the center.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for the inward units' ability to detect looming.

claim: Inward units are sensitive to more hit cases than outward ones.
source: Thus, the inward units are sensitive to more hit cases than the outward ones.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the angular distribution analysis.

claim: The broad inhibition in outward solutions is consistent with the large receptive field of LPi neurons suggested by experiments.
source: This broad inhibition is consistent with the large receptive field of LPi neurons suggested by experiments (Mauss et al., 2015; Klapoetke et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citations to experimental work.

claim: Outward solutions suppress miss and retreat signals better than inward solutions.
source: The outward solutions suppress the miss and retreat signals better, while the inward solutions better suppress rotation signals (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is stated directly with reference to the figure.

claim: Inward solutions better suppress rotation signals compared to outward solutions.
source: The outward solutions suppress the miss and retreat signals better, while the inward solutions better suppress rotation signals (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is stated directly with reference to the figure.

claim: Models with 256 units can more accurately detect hit stimuli than models with 32 units.
source: Both 32 unit and 256 unit models have units covering the entire visual field (Figure 6), but the models with 256 units can more accurately detect hit stimuli (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is stated directly comparing model performance.

claim: Both inward and outward solutions predict higher hit probabilities for near misses than far misses.
source: In some cases, misses can appear very similar to hits if the object passes near the origin. Both inward and outward solutions reflect this in their predictions in response to near misses, which have higher hit probabilities than far misses (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is stated directly with reference to the figure.

claim: For RI models, as the number of units increases, an increasing proportion of solutions have outward filters.
source: For the RI models, on the other hand, as the number of units increases, an increasing proportion of solutions have outward filters (Figure 9—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated directly with reference to the figure.

claim: The form and position of the nonlinearity in the circuit play a role in selecting between different optimized solutions.
source: Combined, these results with LRF and RI models indicate that the form and position of the nonlinearity in the circuit play a role in selecting between different optimized solutions.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from comparing LRF and RI model results.

claim: The outward unit behaves similarly to LPLC2 neurons on many different types of stimuli.
source: The outward unit behaves similarly to LPLC2 neurons on many different types of stimuli.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the comparison results.

claim: The outward unit is selective for loom signals and does not have strong responses to non-looming signals.
source: Not surprisingly, the unit is selective for loom signals and does not have strong responses to non-looming signals (Figure 10B).
evidence: This is stated with reference to the figure showing responses.

claim: The outward unit closely follows the responses of LPLC2 neurons to various expanding bar stimuli, including inhibitory effects of inward motion.
source: Moreover, the unit closely follows the responses of LPLC2 neurons to various expanding bar stimuli, including the inhibitory effects of inward motion (Figure 10C and D).
evidence: This is stated directly comparing model and neural responses.

claim: The outward unit correctly predicts periphery inhibition observed in LPLC2 neurons.
source: In addition, in experiments, motion signals that appear at the periphery of the receptive field suppress the activity of the LPLC2 neurons (periphery inhibition) (Klapoetke et al., 2017), and this phenomenon is successfully predicted by the outward unit (Figure 10E and F) due to its broad inhibitory filters (Figure 10A).
evidence: This is stated directly with citations and figure references.

claim: The outward unit correctly predicts response patterns of LPLC2 neurons for expanding bars with different orientations.
source: The unit also correctly predicts response patterns of the LPLC2 neurons for expanding bars with different orientations (Figure 10G and H).
evidence: This is stated directly with figure references.

claim: The trained model reliably encodes the angular size of the stimulus rather than its angular velocity, despite only having angular velocities as inputs.
source: Surprisingly, although our model only has angular velocities as inputs (Figure 3), it reliably encodes the angular size of the stimulus rather than its angular velocity (Figure 10J).
evidence: This is stated as a surprising finding with figure reference.

claim: The inward solution cannot reproduce the neural data.
source: Not surprisingly, the inward solution cannot reproduce the neural data (Figure 10—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated directly with figure reference.

claim: Training a simple network to detect collisions gives rise to a computation that closely resembles neurons sensitive to looming signals.
source: In this study, we have shown that training a simple network to detect collisions gives rise to a computation that closely resembles neurons that are sensitive to looming signals.
evidence: This is stated as the main conclusion in the Discussion.

claim: One class of optimized solution matched the anatomy of motion inputs to LPLC2 neurons.
source: Specifically, we optimized a neural network model to detect whether an object is on a collision course based on visual motion signals (Figure 3), and found that one class of optimized solution matched the anatomy of motion inputs to LPLC2 neurons (Figures 1, 5 and 6).
evidence: This is stated as a key finding with figure references.

claim: The optimized solution reproduces a wide range of experimental observations of LPLC2 neuron responses.
source: Importantly, this solution reproduces a wide range of experimental observations of LPLC2 neuron responses (Figure 10; Klapoetke et al., 2017; von Reyn et al., 2017; Ache et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citations and figure reference.

claim: For an individual detector unit, an inward structure can make a better loom detector than an outward structure.
source: In particular, for an individual detector unit, an inward structure can make a better loom detector than an outward structure, since it is sensitive to colliding objects originating from a wider array of incoming angles (Figure 7).
evidence: This is stated as a finding with figure reference.

claim: As the number of units across visual space increases, the performance of the outward-sensitive receptive field structure comes to match the performance of the inward solutions.
source: As the number of units across visual space increases, the performance of the outward-sensitive receptive field structure comes to match the performance of the inward solutions (Figure 9, Figure 9—figure supplement 1, Figure 9—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with figure references.

claim: The optimized solutions depend on the number of detectors, likely related to increasing overlap in receptive fields as the population grows.
source: The optimized solutions depend on the number of detectors, and this is likely related to the increasing overlap in receptive fields as the population grows (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated as an inference with figure reference.

claim: Understanding anatomical, physiological, and algorithmic properties of individual neurons can require considering the population response.
source: Thus, understanding anatomical, physiological, and algorithmic properties of individual neurons can require considering the population response.
evidence: This is stated as a general conclusion from the results.

claim: Individual LPLC2 responses should be interpreted in light of the population of LPLC2 responses.
source: The solutions we found to the loom inference problem suggest that individual LPLC2 responses should be interpreted in light of the population of LPLC2 responses.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study.

claim: LPLC2 neurons transform their inputs of direction-selective motion signals to computations of angular size.
source: In particular, these optimized models clarify an interesting but puzzling fact: LPLC2 neurons transform their inputs of direction-selective motion signals to computations of angular size (Ache et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citation to experimental work.

claim: Units of the outward solution exhibit sparsity in their responses to looming stimuli.
source: The units of the outward solution exhibit sparsity in their responses to looming stimuli, in contrast to the denser representations in the inward solution (Figure 8).
evidence: This is stated with figure reference.

claim: Inhibitory circuits play an important role for the selectivity of LPLC2 neurons.
source: Experiments have shown that inhibitory circuits play an important role for the selectivity of LPLC2 neurons.
evidence: This is stated referencing experimental findings.

claim: The strong inhibition on the periphery of the receptive field arises naturally in the outward solutions after optimization.
source: The strong inhibition on the periphery of the receptive field arises naturally in the outward solutions after optimization.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the optimization.

claim: The extent of the inhibitory components increases as more units are added to models.
source: The extent of the inhibitory components increases as more units are added to models (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated with figure reference.

claim: The broad inhibition in the model appears to suppress responses to non-hit stimuli.
source: The broad inhibition appears in our model to suppress responses to the non-hit stimuli, and as in the data, the inhibition is broader than one might expect if the neuron were simply being inhibited by inward motion.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the model behavior.

claim: The larger inhibitory fields in the model are consistent with larger spatial pooling likely supplied by inhibitory LPi inputs.
source: These larger inhibitory fields are also consistent with the larger spatial pooling likely to be supplied by inhibitory LPi inputs (Klapoetke et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citation.
